newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to privatise CNIA insurance firm.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to privatise CNIA insurance firm.

text.p: Morocco has launched an international tender for sale of its majority stake in leading insurance firm Compagnie Nord Africaine et Intercontinentale d'Assurance (CNIA), the Privatisation Ministry said on Tuesday.
"The Privatisation Ministry has mandated the French GP Banque as adviser for the cession of the state stake in CNIA capital," a spokesman told Reuters.
The closing date for the tender is December 17, 1996, he said.
The state holds 1.65 million shares or 78.6 percent stake in the firm.
The decision was a part of "the undergoing government privatisation programme to cede its stakes in 114 enterprises by end 1998."
Morocco privatised more than 46 firms since the plan was launched in November 1993.
Established in Casablanca since 1949, CNIA has a capital of 210 million dirhams.
According to the latest available figures the firm's turnover was 532 million dirhams in 1994, an Upline Securities stockbroker said.
It is the first state-owned insurance company to be sold, he added.
